label: IB Economics Paper 1 · best-fit assessment
descriptorStatus: OEP summaries of the supplied teacher-guide bands; not verbatim official IB descriptors

focus: Address the exact command term and all requested elements
Develop correct causal explanation and analysis
Use and explain diagrams or calculations where the question requires them

bands.description: Fully developed explanation addressing the task, including required diagram or calculation evidence

focus: Apply relevant theory to the question
Develop real-world application when requested, rather than just naming a country
Consider competing arguments and relevant conditions
Sustain balanced evaluation and reach a supported judgment

bands.description: Developed analysis but weak balance or evaluation
Sustained, applied evaluation with a supported judgment

rules: Use holistic best-fit judgment per part; do not add invented criterion weights or marks per keyword.
Use the whole mark range. The top band does not require a flawless answer or every point in an indicative answer.
Select the band first, then the mark within it. Explain the mark with evidence from the submission and the relevant question-specific reference.
Credit economically correct alternative approaches, examples, diagrams and conclusions. Do not compare wording, paragraph order, length or vocabulary overlap with the reference answer.
The supplied references are indicative answer guidance, not graded student exemplars. Do not claim teacher-score calibration or invent benchmark marks.
Judge the stated question and level. Do not demand unrelated advanced or HL-only material for a shared SL/HL question. Difficulty labels must not adjust the marking standard.
Part (a) is explanatory: do not require evaluation unless the actual question calls for it. Part (b) requires analysis and critical evaluation responsive to the command term.
No automatic word-count, spelling, formatting or essay-structure penalties. Do not repeatedly penalize one underlying misconception as unrelated errors.
A named country alone is not developed real-world application. Do not require exact statistics unless the task does. Flag uncertain facts instead of fabricating verification.

Assess diagrams only when available or relevant. This interface supplies text only: a written description is not a verified drawing. Never invent axes or curves or assume unseen diagram evidence. Flag required-but-unseen diagrams in reviewNotes and qualify the mark; do not invent a universal numerical cap.
Question-specific guidance controls task-specific scope and explicitly stated restrictions. Never add arbitrary hard caps. General and question-specific guidance must be interpreted together.
Give positive credit for what is demonstrated, then actionable improvements. Quote only exact student wording as evidence. If no relevant evidence exists, return an empty evidence list.
Do not produce an overall IB 1–7 grade or invent examination-session grade boundaries from this single response.
